page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v5 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the DLSv5 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, configured with 1 physical core and 2 threads per core to deliver 2 vCPUs. The hardware profile includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1889.98 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1589.0. However, multi-core and memory-bound performance is limited. The multi-core stress-ng score is 1932.38, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 1861.0, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds recorded at 14.32 GB/sec and 13.3 GB/sec respectively.

Given the low memory allocation and poor multi-core scaling, this server is not suited for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or complex LLM inference. It is best utilized for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, or simple text processing. It offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated compute resources where high memory capacity and local storage are not required.
